_comment: Transcribed from light-and-etiolation-source-doc.md §G (the ranked list is the single source of truth -- this file derives from it, per BUILD_BRIEF.md §8b, not maintained independently). Items are in NARRATION order (countdown #10 -> #1), matching the order they'll be spoken in script.txt. 'opening_line' values are the ACTUAL WhisperX transcription of manifest.json's scene text, not script.txt's prose spelling -- WhisperX transcribed digits ('Number 10') rather than spelled-out numbers for every item except #3 ('Number three'), confirmed against the real Etiolation_S1 manifest 2026-08-06. 'species' matches the canonical channel_dna/aeonium_glow.json subjects key exactly, for future listicle-mode species-validation authority (BUILD_BRIEF.md §8a.2, not yet wired into the validator).
outro_opening_line: So here is the fix I promised, and here is the part that matters most.
_comment_outro: Marks where the general 'here's the fix' section starts, AFTER item #1 (Echeveria elegans) -- without this, stamp_items.py's last-item span would run to end-of-manifest and silently sweep the whole 18-scene outro into item-01's group, mislabeling generic light-acclimation advice as being about Echeveria specifically. See stamp_items.py's module docstring.

items.twist: Handles low light better than anything else here. That is not the same as liking it.
items.opening_line: Number 10 is Gasteria, sometimes sold as Ox Tongue.

items.twist: It is meant to be tall. That is what lets it get away with it.
It does not fall apart. It grows a neck.
items.opening_line: Number 8 is Haworthiopsis fasciata, the zebra plant, still widely sold as Haworthia fasciata.

items.twist: The fuzz hides the gaps until the gaps are the point.
items.opening_line: Number 7 is Kalanchoe tomentosa, the panda plant.

items.twist: It grows fast either way. Only one of those is growth you want.
items.opening_line: Number 6 is Portulacaria afra, the elephant bush.

items.twist: People think it is finally becoming a tree. It is just reaching.
items.opening_line: Number 5 is Crassula ovata, the jade plant.

items.twist: Gappy pearls look thirsty. They are just dark.
items.opening_line: Number 4 is Curio rowleyanus, String of Pearls, still sold as Senecio rowleyanus.

items.twist: It evolved on a mountainside. You put it on a bookshelf.
items.opening_line: Number three is Sempervivum tectorum, hens and chicks.

items.twist: It does not stretch. It grows a stalk and falls over.
items.opening_line: Number 2 is Lithops, the Living Stones.

items.twist: The shape you bought it for is the first thing it loses.
items.opening_line: Number 1 is Echeveria elegans, the Mexican snowball.
